best_for: Developers who switch between Windows, macOS and Linux and want one terminal with built-in tabs, panes and SSH, set up in a Lua file they can carry between machines.
description:
WezTerm is a terminal emulator, the window your command-line shell runs in, written by Wez Furlong.

You can search back through everything a session printed with Ctrl-Shift-F, and scroll with the mouse wheel or Shift-PageUp. The config file reloads the moment you save it, so you see a change without restarting. Text shows in bold, italic, strikethrough and double underline, and color schemes can change on the fly. Beyond its own image command, it also shows pictures sent with the Kitty graphics method, and with Sixel as an experimental option. Mouse reporting works inside vim and tmux, and you can paste a selection with Shift-Insert.

points.title: A multiplexer built in
points.text: Tabs, split panes and windows are part of the terminal, and they can run on remote hosts as well as locally. If you use tmux mainly to split the screen, you may not need it here.

points.title: Configured in Lua
points.text: Settings live in a Lua file rather than a settings screen. That makes your setup easy to copy and version, but there is little to click if you prefer menus.

points.title: SSH and serial without extra tools
points.text: `wezterm ssh` opens a remote session directly, and `wezterm serial` connects to serial ports, such as an Arduino. It also shows inline images with `wezterm imgcat` and supports font ligatures and color emoji.

points.title: The stable build dates from 2024
points.text: The current stable release is 20240203-110809. Newer work ships only as nightly builds, offered as a Windows installer and zip, a Homebrew cask (`wezterm@nightly`), an AppImage and Linux repositories. This site lists the stable line.

points.title: Windows 10 1809 or newer
points.text: WezTerm needs 64-bit Windows 10 build 17763 or later because it relies on the Pseudo Console. The listed installer needs admin rights and adds WezTerm to PATH; a zip from the project runs without installing.

points.title: The Flatpak has sandbox limits
points.text: The Flathub build is published by Wez Furlong and marked verified. The project warns that the sandbox breaks some features, such as reading a pane's current folder, and suggests a native package once you settle on WezTerm.

points.title: Versions kept here
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 17 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source. The Mac build is a single universal app for Intel and Apple silicon. WezTerm is free under the MIT license.
